unit.label: Renting & rooms
unit.title: A Place to Rent
unit.description: Begin this lesson with renting and the home: landlords, rooms, left/right location, nearby places, walking time, 來 + activity, and the single-sentence 就 that marks unexpectedly little time or distance.

goal.text: 我來看房子。走路五分鐘就到了。
goal.pinyin: Wǒ lái kàn fángzi. Zǒulù wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
goal.meaning: I came to look at the place. It is only a five-minute walk to get there.

unit.bookReference: A Course in Contemporary Chinese 1 · Lesson 11 Dialogue I / Vocabulary I (printed pp. 224–226) and Grammar I–II (printed pp. 230–232). Unit 32 completes Dialogue I, including 回去想想，再打電話給你; transparent combinations remain taught in context rather than being inflated into separate core targets.

lessons.title: A Place to Rent
lessons.subtitle: Start this lesson with the core rental words: 租, 房東, 套房, and the 房 character family.

lessons.title: Living Room, Kitchen, Bathroom

lessons.title: Left, Right, and Vacant Rooms
lessons.subtitle: Use 左邊 / 右邊, count rooms with 間, and use 空 for a vacant room.

steps.prompt: In 兩間空房間, what does 間 do?
steps.explanation: 間 is the measure word for rooms and houses here.

steps.prompt: What does 空 mean in 空房間?
steps.explanation: Here 空 kōng describes a vacant room. Earlier 有空 used kòng in the expression 'to be free'.

lessons.title: Nearby on Foot

lessons.title: Come Here to Do It
lessons.subtitle: Contrast 來 + activity with the earlier 去 + activity pattern, and add 電話 for contacting the landlord.

steps.explanation: 空 kōng describes a vacant room here.

newVocabulary.meaning: measure word for rooms and houses

newVocabulary.note: Orders a later action in the source conversation: 想想，再打電話.
the vocabulary set lists 房間 as the ordinary noun for a room; 房 and 間 are now both familiar.
The landlord says 請進 at the start of the conversation. 進 means to enter/go in.

租.note: 租 is first-tone zū. In this lesson it is the verb “to rent,” especially a room or apartment.
租.memory: 禾 forms the five-stroke left side; 且 forms the five-stroke right side. Keep the two blocks narrow and balanced.

parts.label: 禾
parts.name: grain component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 禾 on the left.

parts.label: 且
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final five strokes form 且, with its stacked horizontal lines, on the right.

房.note: 房 is the first character of 房子, house. Notice the upper-left 戶 and the 方 beneath it.
房.memory: 房 shelters 方 beneath 戶. The long left stroke of 戶 runs down beside the lower group.

parts.label: 戶
parts.name: door-shaped upper group
parts.description: 戶 begins above 方, then its long sloping stroke extends down the left side of the lower group.

parts.label: 方
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: 方 sits underneath the upper part of 戶. Leave room for its hooked and slanting strokes below the horizontal.

房.partOrderLabel: 戶 first, then 方 below

客.meaning: guest; first character of 客廳
客.note: 客 is fourth-tone kè. In 客廳 it is part of the word for living room.
客.memory: 宀 is the three-stroke roof; 各 fills the lower space with a crossing top above 口.

parts.label: 宀
parts.name: roof component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 宀 across the top.

parts.label: 各
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 各 under the roof.

廚.meaning: kitchen; first character of 廚房
廚.note: 廚 is second-tone chú. Learn it as the first character of 廚房, “kitchen.”
廚.memory: 广 makes a three-stroke shelter; the remaining 尌-shaped body fills the inside without crossing the left shelter.

parts.label: 广
parts.name: shelter component
parts.description: The first three strokes form the sloping 广 shelter.

parts.label: 尌
parts.name: inner body
parts.description: The remaining twelve strokes build the dense inner body beneath 广.

左.note: 左 gives the left direction. Notice 工 below the upper strokes.
左.memory: Look for 工 under the overhanging top of 左; compare the 口 in 右.

parts.label: 𠂇
parts.name: upper strokes
parts.description: The first two strokes form a horizontal top and a long slant down to the left.

parts.label: 工
parts.name: work-shaped part
parts.description: 工 has two horizontal lines joined by a short vertical. It distinguishes 左 from 右.

右.note: 右 gives the right direction. Notice 口 below the upper strokes. Follow the guide: its opening stroke order differs from 左.
右.memory: Look for 口 under the overhanging top of 右; compare the 工 in 左.

parts.label: 𠂇
parts.name: upper strokes
parts.description: The first two strokes form the overhanging top and the slant down to the left.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth-shaped part
parts.description: 口 is the small box below the top strokes. It distinguishes 右 from 左.

浴.meaning: bathe; first character of 浴室
浴.note: 浴 is fourth-tone yù. In 浴室 it is part of the word for bathroom.
浴.memory: Three water dots 氵 stay narrow on the left; 谷 fills the right with spreading upper strokes above 口.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 氵.

parts.label: 谷
parts.name: valley component
parts.description: The final seven strokes form 谷 on the right.

超.meaning: surpass; first character of 超商
超.note: 超 is the first character of 超商, the everyday Taiwan word for a convenience store.
超.memory: 走 + 召: the familiar 走 stretches underneath 召, which has 刀 above 口.

parts.label: 走
parts.name: walking component
parts.description: 走 occupies the left side and sends its long final stroke underneath the right component.

parts.label: 召
parts.name: upper-right component
parts.description: 召 is 刀 above 口. Nest this smaller group above the long base of 走.

超.partOrderLabel: wrapping 走, then inner 召

走.note: 走 means walk; in a directions question it asks how to get somewhere.
走.memory: Remember 走 by 土 above a long, spreading lower stroke.

parts.label: 土
parts.name: upper shape
parts.description: The upper three strokes form a 土 shape: a vertical crossing two horizontal lines.

parts.label: 龰
parts.name: lower group
parts.description: The lower group leads down to the long final stroke sweeping out to the right.

路.note: 路 means road. 路口 means an intersection.
路.memory: Remember 路 as 足 + 各: a small mouth above foot strokes on the left, and a crossing top above 口 on the right.

parts.label: 足
parts.name: foot component
parts.description: 足 forms the left side, with 口 at the top and the foot-shaped strokes below.

parts.label: 各
parts.name: right part
parts.description: 各 has crossing, spreading strokes at the top and a small 口 underneath.

間.note: 間 is first-tone jiān here. It counts rooms and houses: 兩間房間.
間.memory: The eight-stroke 門 surrounds a four-stroke 日. Keep the inner 日 centered with space around it.

parts.label: 門
parts.name: door frame
parts.description: The first eight strokes form the Traditional door frame 門.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: sun component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 日 inside the frame.

套.meaning: set; first character of 套房
套.note: 套 is fourth-tone tào. 套房 is a suite: a room with its own bathroom in this lesson.
套.memory: 大 spreads across the top; 镸 fills the lower seven strokes and stays centered under it.

parts.label: 大
parts.name: big component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 大.

parts.label: 镸
parts.name: long component
parts.description: The final seven strokes form the lower component.

再.note: 再 is fourth-tone zài. In this lesson it orders a later action: think first, then call.
再.memory: A single top bar sits over 冉. The lower frame is crossed by a central vertical and finishes with the long horizontal.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: top bar
parts.description: Begin with the single horizontal roof.

parts.label: 冉
parts.name: lower structure
parts.description: The remaining five strokes form 冉 below the roof.

話.note: 話 is fourth-tone huà. It appears in 電話 and 打電話.
話.memory: 言 forms the seven-stroke left side; 舌 forms the six-stroke right side with 口 at the bottom.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form 言.

parts.label: 舌
parts.name: tongue component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 舌.

進.note: 進 is fourth-tone jìn. In 請進, it means enter / come in.
進.memory: Write the eight-stroke 隹 body first, then add the four-stroke movement component 辶 wrapping along the lower-left.

parts.label: 隹
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form 隹, the compact inner body.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: movement component
parts.description: The final four strokes form the Traditional movement component 辶 around the lower-left.

進.partOrderLabel: inner 隹, then wrapping 辶

u32-lai-vp.title: Come here to do something
u32-lai-vp.explanation: 來 + VP says that the subject comes toward the speaker or the relevant deictic location in order to do the activity. It parallels the earlier 去 + activity pattern, but the direction is toward rather than away. Negation, auxiliary verbs, and adverbs go before 來: 不來上課, 要來看房子, 常來游泳. Do not use 來 merely as a generic future marker.

examples.meaning: I came here to study Chinese.
He came here to play basketball.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào lái kàn fángzi ma?
examples.meaning: Are you coming to look at the place?
I am not coming to class tomorrow.

u32-lai-vp.remember: 來 points toward the relevant location; 去 points away. Put 不, 要, 常 and similar words before 來.

u32-early-jiu.title: Sooner than expected with 就
u32-early-jiu.explanation: In a time or distance context, 就 can present an event as occurring sooner, more directly, or with less delay than expected: 走路五分鐘就到了. This is different from the linking 就 in 要是…就…: here the sentence can stand alone without a condition. Sentence-final 了 often appears with arrival or change, but it is not required in every 就 sentence.

examples.pinyin: Zǒulù wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
examples.meaning: It is only a five-minute walk to get there.
He will be here in just a moment.

examples.text: 那個地方很近，很快就到了。
examples.pinyin: Nàge dìfang hěn jìn, hěn kuài jiù dào le.
examples.meaning: That place is close; you get there very quickly.

u32-early-jiu.remember: Here 就 signals unexpectedly little time or distance. Do not automatically treat every 就 as the consequence half of 要是…就….

u32-rent.meaning: I want to rent a suite.
u32-rent.note: 租 is the verb rent; 套房 here is a suite/room with its own bathroom.

u32-landlord.text: 還有兩間空房間，一間是套房，一間不是。
u32-landlord.pinyin: Hái yǒu liǎng jiān kōng fángjiān, yì jiān shì tàofáng, yì jiān bú shì.
u32-landlord.meaning: There are two other vacant rooms. One is a suite, and one is not.
u32-landlord.note: This keeps the the conversation wording. 還有 here means 'there are also/still'; 間 counts rooms and 空 kōng means vacant.

u32-rooms.text: 這裡是客廳，廚房在左邊，右邊有浴室。
u32-rooms.pinyin: Zhèlǐ shì kètīng, chúfáng zài zuǒbiān, yòubiān yǒu yùshì.
u32-rooms.meaning: This is the living room. The kitchen is on the left, and there is a bathroom on the right.
u32-rooms.note: This preserves the room layout from the conversation; the living room itself is not said to be on the left.

u32-kitchen.meaning: The kitchen is on the left.

u32-market.meaning: Nearby there are a supermarket and an MRT station.
u32-market.note: the conversation describes the rental environment with both a supermarket and an MRT station.

u32-walk.pinyin: Zǒulù wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
u32-walk.meaning: It is only a five-minute walk to get there.
u32-walk.note: 分鐘 is transparent here from the already learned 分 'minute' plus 鐘; 就 presents the arrival as sooner/easier than expected.

u32-phone.note: 打電話 is the ordinary collocation 'make a phone call'. Here 給 is the this lesson preposition 'to', marking the recipient: 打電話給房東. Compare earlier 給你一塊水果, where 給 is the verb 'give'.

u32-come-house.meaning: I came here to look at the place.
u32-come-house.note: 來 + activity means coming toward the relevant location to do the activity.

u32-come-class.meaning: I am not coming to class tomorrow.
u32-come-class.note: The negative 不 goes before 來.

u32-come-question.pinyin: Nǐ yào lái kàn fángzi ma?
u32-come-question.meaning: Are you coming to look at the place?
u32-come-question.note: 要 appears before 來, the first verbal element.

u32-quick.meaning: He will be here in just a moment.
u32-quick.note: This 就 presents the event as happening sooner than expected.

u32-place.text: 房子很不錯，這裡很方便。
u32-place.pinyin: Fángzi hěn búcuò, zhèlǐ hěn fāngbiàn.
u32-place.meaning: The place is pretty good, and this area is very convenient.
u32-place.note: Both 不錯 and 方便 are previously learned words reused directly from the conversation.

u32-internet.meaning: Can you access the internet from the room?
u32-internet.note: the conversation reuses 裡面, 可以 and 上網 while practicing the new rental noun 房間.

u32-opinion.text: 你覺得這間房間怎麼樣？你想租嗎？
u32-opinion.pinyin: Nǐ juéde zhè jiān fángjiān zěnmeyàng? Nǐ xiǎng zū ma?
u32-opinion.meaning: What do you think of this room? Do you want to rent it?
u32-opinion.note: This keeps the landlord's evaluation-and-decision sequence from the conversation, using neutral 你 in the practice version.
tokens: 你覺得這間房間怎麼樣

u32-return-call.text: 我回去想想，再打電話給你。
u32-return-call.pinyin: Wǒ huíqù xiǎngxiang, zài dǎ diànhuà gěi nǐ.
u32-return-call.meaning: I'll go back and think about it, then call you.
u32-return-call.note: This is the closing move of the conversation. Here 想想 means 'think it over', extending earlier 想 + VP 'want to'. 再 orders the later action, and 給 in 打電話給你 marks the call recipient.

u32-occupied.note: the conversation previews existential 有 here. Unit 33 explains the indefinite-subject grammar formally.

u32-come-in.note: This restores the landlord's opening line from the conversation. The understood subject is 你; Unit 33 reuses this exact example for zero-pronoun omission.
